audit.why: Ranged skirmish-mage with two repositioning tools (Across the Veil W 22/21/20/19/18, The Weirding E 15/14/13/12/11) against a melee drain bruiser. Aurora owns the walk-up until her W is spent; Aatrox owns any extended trade from level 3, and the 46.31% win rate over 149 games matches that.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 phase named her ultimate as "Between the Worlds" — that ability does not exist — and gave no cooldown for either ultimate.
audit.why: Riot's kit file names it Between Worlds (R) at 140/120/100 seconds. Aatrox's World Ender is 120/100/80, so at rank 1 he can spend his ultimate 20 seconds more often than you can spend yours. That gap is what makes a traded 6-spike bad for Aurora.
audit.corrected: Between Worlds (R, 140s) zones his all-in and lets you blink across the rift. World Ender is 120s and out-drains your chip — spend R only on his commit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers claim Across the Veil makes Aurora "untargetable" to Aatrox. Riot's text says it makes her invisible — a different mechanic, and one that a facing check or a point-blank swing still beats. The decisive interaction (Infernal Chains dragging her back to the impact centre) was described as a slow zone rather than the drag it is, and Umbral Dash was never mentioned at all.
audit.why: Across the Veil (W): 'entering the spirit realm upon landing, becoming invisible.' No untargetability anywhere in her kit. Infernal Chains (W, 20/18/16/14/12): champions 'have to leave the impact area quickly or they will be dragged to the center and take the damage again' — leaving the circle is the counterplay, not tanking it. Umbral Dash (E) is 9/8/7/6/5, by far his shortest cooldown, so it is his re-stick after you leap; leaping before it is spent wastes a 22s cooldown against a 9s one. Deathbringer Stance (P) is an auto-attack reset and it heals off your max health, so his wind-up — not his ability cast — is the cue to step back, and Grievous Wounds decides every long trade.
audit.corrected: Q3's sweetspot edge knocks up — sidestep it. Infernal Chains drags you back unless you leave the zone fast.

audit.whatIsWrong: No line told the player which of Aatrox's cooldowns is the punishable one.
audit.why: Umbral Dash at 9s (rank 1) is his only re-engage once Across the Veil has broken his stick. Leaping after he spends it is the whole trade pattern.
audit.corrected: Across the Veil (22s at rank 1) breaks his Q3 sweetspot; he re-sticks with Umbral Dash on 9s, so leap after that dash, not before.

audit.why: Itemization already calls for early Oblivion Orb / Executioner's, which is right: Deathbringer Stance (P), Umbral Dash (E) and World Ender (R) all heal him.

edits.after: Between Worlds (R, 140s) zones his all-in and lets you blink across the rift. World Ender is 120s and out-drains chip — save R for his commit.

notes: Two derived flags in champ-data/_kits/aatrox.json contradict Riot's own description and I did not use them: Infernal Chains is flagged 'grounding' but the description only says enemies are dragged to the centre (no dash lockout), and World Ender is flagged 'revealsStealth' but the description only lists minion fear, AD, healing and Move Speed. Since Across the Veil's escape is invisibility, whether World Ender reveals it is the single most important unknown in this matchup — flagged in unverified rather than asserted.
